{{nihongo|'''Hanoura Shrine'''|羽浦神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Hanoura-chō Nakashō|Q28686981|qid=Q28686981}}, {{ill|Anan, Tokushima|Q485583|qid=Q485583}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|Q160734|qid=Q160734}}. {{nihongo|'''Hanoura Shrine'''|羽浦神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Awa Province (Tokushima)]].

== History ==
In {{ill|1890|Q7832|qid=Q7832}} ({{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 43), 23 shrines including Waya Shrine, formerly worshiped in old Nakashō village and old Miyakura village, were merged into village shrine Hachiman Shrine, and it was renamed Hanoura Shrine. In {{ill|1937|Q18647|qid=Q18647}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 12), it was promoted to gōsha.

Hachiman Shrine was visited around {{ill|1586|Q6739|qid=Q6739}} in the {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} era by {{ill|Hachisuka Iemasa|Q1073557|qid=Q1073557}} for domestic peace, lasting family fortune, and safety in falconry; in {{ill|1603|Q6735|qid=Q6735}} ({{ill|Keichō|ca|Keichō|es|Keichō|fa|کیچو (دوره)|fr|Ère Keichō|id|Keichō|it|Keichō|ja|慶長|ko|게이초|ru|Кэйтё|simple|Keichō|sr|Кеичо|sv|Keichō|th|เคโช|tr|Keichō|uk|Кейтьо|zh|慶長|qid=Q1328185}} 8), {{ill|Hachisuka Yoshishige|Q3125481|qid=Q3125481}} designated it a prayer shrine of the Hachisuka family.

Waya Shrine is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} and was listed in the Jinmyōchō of the {{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}} in the era of {{ill|Emperor Daigo|Q329753|qid=Q329753}}.
